To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TCP throughput depends on the round-trip-time, the receiver advertised window and the congestion window growth rate.

the window size evolution of TCP connections can be modeled by a Markov chain, that the throughput of TCP can be predicted using the Markov chain and that the model predicts well the throughput of real TCP connections.
the throughput of TCP connections can be accurately predicted by the proposed model for a wide range of round-trip times and that the throughput is a decreasing function of the round-trip delay.
In summary, our research is concerned with
modeling TCP in the presence of sublinear window growth and receiver limitations.
the modeling and the analytical characterization of the performance of a TCP connection in the presence of nonlinearity in the window size growth.
the modeling and analysis of TCP connections in the presence of sublinear window growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed TCP modeling approach provides a very good fit to the TCP throughput measured over real networks.

the model proposed here is a useful tool for understanding the behavior of TCP in the presence of nonlinearity and limitation, as well as for predicting the performance of the protocol in a wide range of scenarios.
the model presented is the best available model of the TCP protocol in the presence of sublinear window growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the throughput of TCP can be predicted with good precision if the sublinear window growth is accounted for.
we have developed a TCP model that accounts for sublinearity and receiver window limitation.
we have developed a TCP model that is able to predict the throughput for different window growth functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sublinearity and limitations on window growth are important to model accurately the throughput of TCP.
the throughput predicted by our model is higher than the one predicted by models that do not account for the limitation.
sublinear window growth and receiver window limitation have to be accounted for when analyzing the performance of a TCP connection.
